conventions.convention: The generator set may be infinite. Bruhat order is the finite-chain closure of length-increasing right multiplication by conjugates of simple generators.
Coefficients lie in Z[Γ] for a translation-invariant totally ordered abelian group Γ; the negative part uses strictly negative exponents. General weight functions have no sign restriction.
The quadratic relation is (T_s−v^{L(s)})(T_s+v^{−L(s)})=0; finite Coxeter labels impose braid relations and infinite labels impose none.
A nonzero C_x coefficient in C_sC_y means x ←_L y and x ≤_L y. The quotient retains the cell inside its downward preorder span.

A canonical basic set is relative to the specified free stable lattices and integer statistic α. Each column has a unique least-α contributing label, with multiplicity one; arbitrary local-order lattice independence is not assumed.

The modular regime assumes finite Weyl W, nonnegative integral L, split H_Q(v), and the explicitly written P2–P8 and P15′. L-good means every leading Schur integer f_E remains nonzero, rather than every full Schur element.
D_w=C_w^dagger with T_s^dagger=−T_s^{-1}; asymptotic layers use D_w, and their cell quotients are dagger twists of native C-basis cell modules. The multiplicative parameter is ξ=θ(v)^2.
The complete local modular-system construction assumes AC and uses R equal to the completion of A at ker θ, with residue field Frac(θ(A)); the specialization field may extend that residue field.

load_bearing.statement: Under the specified finite-Weyl data, P2–P8 and P15′, J is an associative integral algebra with the stated identity, anti-involution and perfect trace. Its a-layers identify with the free Hecke layers as (J_A,H)-bimodules; natural left H action is restriction through the displayed unital homomorphism φ. The kernel after every commutative specialization is nilpotent, φ_Q(v) is an isomorphism, and J_Q is split semisimple with uniquely supported rational simples.

Under the specified finite-Weyl hypotheses, the rational J-simples have positive integral leading Schur coefficients f_E and support degrees ν_E=α_E, with c_E(v)=f_E v^{−2ν_E} plus higher powers and c_E(v) in A. Integral free J-stable lattices give a full matrix decomposition after inverting the f_E, surviving arbitrary commutative base change. Restriction through φ constructs globally free Hecke models.

Assuming AC, the specified finite-Weyl hypotheses and a characteristic-zero or L-good specialization, the explicit free models give d_{E,M}=[*V_E:M], independently of other free stable R-models and unchanged by residue-field extension. For H_ke a projective cover of M, the multiplicity of V_E in B_i e is d_{E,M} when i=α_E and zero otherwise.

For any Coxeter generator set, each finite-generator restricted Coxeter presentation embeds with intrinsic length equal to ambient length. Bruhat comparison is equivalent to a reduced subword in any fixed reduced expression; lower intervals have at most 2^{length(w)} elements. Simple multiplication changes length by ±1 on either side.

For every Coxeter generator set and every weight function into a totally ordered abelian group, there is a unique bar-invariant basis C_w=T_w+Σ_{y<w}p_{y,w}T_y with all p_{y,w} in A_<0. For simple s the correction is v^{−L(s)}, zero, or −v^{L(s)} according as L(s) is positive, zero, or negative.

Assuming AC, the completion R of A_{ker θ} is a complete separated Noetherian local domain containing A injectively, with residue Frac(θ(A)). Finite projective R-modules are free; idempotents lift in finite R-algebras; projected free filtration layers retain exactness under fraction and residue base change; finite free modules over an integral split matrix algebra preserve simple multiplicities between these fibres.

Assuming AC, finite Weyl W, nonnegative integral L, the specified generic splitting and P2–P8/P15′, every characteristic-zero or L-good field specialization has split H_k and a unique canonical basic set for the supplied free-model decomposition matrix. Its injection M↦E(M) has multiplicity one and uniquely least Schur exponent in each column; full Schur elements may vanish.
